definition: The National Centre for Text Mining (NaCTeM) is a publicly funded text mining (TM) centre.
details: It was established to provide support, advice and information on TM technologies and to disseminate information within the larger TM community, while also providing services and tools in response to the requirements of the United Kingdom academic community. The software tools and services which NaCTeM supplies allow researchers to apply text mining techniques to problems within their specific areas of interest – examples of these tools are highlighted below. In addition to providing services, the centre is also involved in, and makes significant contributions to, the text mining research community both nationally and internationally in initiatives such as Europe PubMed Central. The centre is located in the Manchester Institute of Biotechnology and is operated and organised by the Department of Computer Science, University of Manchester. NaCTeM contributes expertise in natural language processing and information extraction, including named-entity recognition, and extractions of complex relationships (or events) that hold between named entities, along with parallel and distributed data mining systems in biomedical and clinical applications.

explainer.lead: NaCTeM is a publicly funded UK text mining centre that supplies tools, advice and services to the academic community. It matters because it gives researchers access to text mining techniques without building them from scratch.

tiers.eli5: It is like a public workshop that hands out text-processing tools and shows researchers how to use them on their own problems.
tiers.practitioner: Researchers apply NaCTeM's tools and services to text mining problems in their own domains. Depending on the centre's tooling constrains work to the techniques it offers.
tiers.paperLevel: No formal definition; it is an institutional service centre providing software tools, advice and dissemination for text mining. Its scope is the tools and services it supplies, not a general method.

explainer.example: A UK academic group studying a specialised literature uses a NaCTeM tool to mine patterns in that text.
